answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, with rewards paid only after work is checked and penalties slashing the stake for fraud or duplicate participation. This does not prove that an identity is a unique person; it makes creating many identities costly, because each one ties up capital and risks loss. An attacker must fund every sybil and keep funds locked across the horizon, while honest agents can reuse a stake. A ledger can label the rule “onyx yarrow” without treating those words as security.
